candidates.source_name: IMF Kosovo Technical Assistance Report — Financial Sector Stability Review (2020) and FSSR Follow-up (2026)
candidates.why_relevant: Supranational diagnostic of Kosovo's financial sector including payment system oversight, supervisory IT/data capacity, macroprudential tooling and reform roadmap. Names concrete gaps and planned reforms with dates — the strategic 'why now' for payment-infrastructure vendors. The 2020 FSSR plus the 2026 follow-up give a before/after delta on what CBK actually implemented.
candidates.legal_status: IMF copyright, redistribution restricted; citation and internal analysis permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic (quarterly) crawl of imf.org Kosovo country page + Technical Assistance Reports listing; download PDFs; diff against previous editions to extract reform commitments and named systems (KIPS, SEPA, RTGS).
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query + snowball to IMF eLibrary
queries_used: IMF Kosovo Financial Sector Stability Review payment system

candidates.source_name: IMF Article IV / Stand-By Arrangement & RSF review documents for Kosovo
candidates.why_relevant: SBA/RSF review staff reports carry structural benchmarks that frequently include payment-system and CBK regulatory milestones (Law on Payment Services, cash operations regulation, SEPA preparation). These are the schedule against which vendor-relevant procurement follows.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor IMF country page RSS/press releases; pull each review PDF; extract structural benchmark tables.
queries_used: IMF Kosovo Financial Sector Stability Review payment system

candidates.source_name: European Commission Kosovo Report (annual enlargement package, SWD) — Chapter 4/9 financial services
candidates.why_relevant: The 2025 SWD documents the status of Law 08/L-304 on Banks, Law 08/L-328 on Payment Services and the AML amendment law (all pending Constitutional Court review), and SEPA pre-application status. Authoritative, dated, citable statements on the legal preconditions for payment-market entry.
candidates.access_status: public PDF (ecoi.net mirror is easier to fetch than the EC portal)
candidates.legal_status: EU public document, reuse permitted with attribution (Decision 2011/833/EU)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual (Oct/Nov) fetch of the enlargement package SWD from EC neighbourhood-enlargement site with ecoi.net as fallback mirror; section-extract 'financial services', 'payment', 'SEPA', 'digitalisation'.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query, followed to full SWD PDF
queries_used: European Commission Kosovo Report 2025 chapter financial services payment systems SEPA

candidates.source_name: World Bank Documents & Reports — Kosovo Financial Sector Strengthening / Financial Sector Development Project (P507881) and retail payment cost study
candidates.why_relevant: World Bank project appraisal documents and implementation status reports for Kosovo's financial sector name the specific components being financed — deposit insurance capacity, instant/faster payments, retail payment infrastructure — and often list SECO-funded technical assistance to CBK. PADs are the earliest public signal of donor-funded payment infrastructure spend, which precedes vendor tenders.
candidates.legal_status: CC-BY for most World Bank publications
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Use the World Bank Documents & Reports API filtered by country=Kosovo and majdocType=Project Documents; also track project IDs P507881 and the earlier Financial Sector Strengthening project for ISR updates.
queries_used: World Bank Kosovo Financial Sector Assessment Program payment services report

candidates.source_name: World Bank feature/analysis on SEPA for the Western Balkans
candidates.why_relevant: Benchmarks Kosovo against regional peers on cross-border payment cost and SEPA readiness; useful framing and quantified savings claims for the 'why now' narrative.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch; monitor World Bank ECA blog/feature feed for Western Balkans payments.
queries_used: European Commission Kosovo Report 2025 chapter financial services payment systems SEPA

candidates.source_name: IEG / World Bank Group Country Program Evaluation — Kosovo FY2012-25
candidates.why_relevant: Independent retrospective evaluation of what World Bank financial-sector interventions in Kosovo actually delivered — a rare candid account of failed/stalled components, useful for judging whether announced payment modernisation actually happened.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch of approach paper and final CPE when published.
queries_used: World Bank Kosovo Financial Sector Assessment Program payment services report

candidates.source_name: BIS Central Bankers' Speeches — Ahmet Ismaili (CBK Governor) on SEPA and IMF reviews
candidates.why_relevant: BIS mirrors CBK governor speeches in a stable, fetchable, permanently archived form. Speeches state payment-system strategy, KIPS modernisation intent and SEPA timelines in plain language — and survive even when the CBK site reorganises.
candidates.access_status: public, plain HTML + PDF, very crawlable
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query bis.org/review by author 'Ismaili' and keyword 'Kosovo'; scheduled monthly crawl.
queries_used: IMF Kosovo Financial Sector Stability Review payment system
European Commission Kosovo Report 2025 chapter financial services payment systems SEPA

candidates.source_name: Riinvest Institute for Development Research — banking sector studies (Sektori bankar në Kosovë)
candidates.why_relevant: Kosovo's most established economic think tank; publishes Albanian-language studies on the banking sector, lending costs, competition/concentration and digitalisation. Their reports name banks, quantify market structure and are frequently the local evidence base cited by media and donors.
candidates.legal_status: no explicit open licence; attribution-based citation assumed acceptable
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the publications and 'riinvest-story' sections in Albanian and English; harvest /uploads/files/ PDF paths; keyword filter on 'bankar', 'pagesa', 'digjitalizim', 'fintech'.
queries_used: Riinvest Institute studim sektori bankar Kosovë digjitalizim pagesat

candidates.source_name: GAP Institute for Advanced Studies (Instituti GAP)
candidates.why_relevant: Policy think tank publishing short, data-driven Albanian-language briefs on public spending, consumer protection and banking fees. Frequently analyses public procurement and public-institution IT spend, which is a pointer to vendor contracts.
candidates.access_status: public; site structure requires navigating publications listing
candidates.legal_status: no explicit licence; cite with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl publications index in sq and en; also mirror their LinkedIn posts which sometimes carry the only direct PDF link.
queries_used: GAP Institute Kosovo raport bankat komisionet pagesave

candidates.source_name: Zyra Kombëtare e Auditimit (ZKA) — National Audit Office of Kosovo, IT audit reports
candidates.why_relevant: ZKA performs information-technology audits of Kosovo public systems (SIMFK treasury/financial management system, payroll management system, civil registry ARC, business registration system 2025-2026). These reports describe system architecture, contracted suppliers, security weaknesses and project management failures in named detail — one of the richest public sources on who supplies government IT and how it performs.
candidates.legal_status: official public documents of the Republic of Kosovo; reuse permitted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of the reports listing and /News/NewsArticle/ pages; harvest /cms/ReportFiles/*.pdf; keyword filter 'teknologjisë së informacionit', 'sistemi informativ', 'kontraktori', 'furnizuesi'.
queries_used: Zyra Kombëtare e Auditimit Kosovë raport auditimi sistemet e teknologjisë së informacionit

candidates.source_name: Bank external-audit reports: 'Pasqyrat financiare dhe Raporti i Auditorit të Pavarur' (Big Four audited statements of Kosovo banks/CBK)
candidates.why_relevant: Audited annual statements carry the audit firm's identity, IT/intangible asset notes (core banking and payment software capitalisation), operating-lease and supplier commitments, and related-party disclosures — often the only public quantification of a bank's technology spend. CBK's own audited statements do the same for the central bank.
candidates.source_subtype: external audit report / statutory financial statements
candidates.access_status: public PDFs on bank and CBK websites; not centrally indexed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Per-bank crawl of 'Raporte vjetore' / 'Pasqyrat financiare' sections for each licensed bank on the CBK register; also site-search the Albanian phrase 'Raporti i Auditorit të Pavarur' restricted to .com/.org Kosovo bank domains; parse intangible-assets and commitments notes.
queries_used: "raport i auditorit të pavarur" bankë Kosovë pasqyrat financiare PwC Deloitte KPMG EY 2025

candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API — recovery of removed Kosovo bank, CBK, vendor and procurement pages
candidates.why_relevant: Recovery layer for the whole cell. Kosovo bank and vendor sites are frequently redesigned and press releases/reference pages deleted; CDX enumeration recovers deleted PDF paths (annual reports, tender attachments, vendor reference lists, partnership press releases) that are the only named evidence of contracts. Confirmed working against bqk-kos.org and e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net.
candidates.access_status: public API, rate-limited; occasional 5xx/429 under load
candidates.legal_status: public archive; respect rate limits and robots exclusions
candidates.suggested_collection_method: For each actor domain, run CDX with collapse=urlkey and filter=mimetype:application/pdf plus statuscode:200; diff live sitemap vs CDX to isolate removed URLs; fetch snapshots via /web/{timestamp}id_/{url}. Throttle to ~1 req/s.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct API probe (curl) confirming enumeration works for Kosovo domains
queries_used: cdx api bqk-kos.org
cdx api e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net

candidates.source_name: Archive.today (archive.ph) — snapshot recovery for JS-heavy / paywalled Kosovo media and bank pages

candidates.access_status: public but aggressively bot-defended (Cloudflare interstitial common)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/low-volume lookup as a fallback after Wayback fails; expect CAPTCHA — do not attempt to bypass, queue for human review.
candidates.discovered_via_method: domain knowledge, listed as recovery fallback

negative_findings.description: Searched for Big Four (Deloitte/PwC/KPMG/EY) market studies with an explicit Kosovo banking or payments chapter. Deloitte's Digital Banking Maturity and CE Banking Outlook, and the CEE PSD2 surveys, were the only recurring products found, and none of the retrieved material evidenced Kosovo in the country sample.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Kosovo-specific Big Four banking market study located in this run; only regional CEE/SEE products whose Kosovo coverage is unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If no Big Four Kosovo study exists, the consultancy/benchmark layer for this market rests on IFI reports (IMF/World Bank/EC) and local think tanks (Riinvest/GAP) instead — which changes both the evidence base and the credibility ceiling of any market sizing.

negative_findings.description: Albanian-phrase searching for 'Raporti i Auditorit të Pavarur' plus 'bankë' surfaced audited statements for NGOs, political entities, KOSTT, the Insurance Bureau, FINCA and the CBK — but no central index of commercial-bank audited statements, and nothing dated 2025.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bank external-audit reports exist but are scattered across individual bank websites with no aggregator; recent-year coverage was not reachable through general search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection must be per-bank (walk the CBK register of licensed banks and crawl each 'Raporte vjetore' section) rather than search-driven, and Wayback CDX will be needed for years whose PDFs were rotated off the live sites.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200/200) was consumed before planned queries on EBRD/IFC Kosovo banking diagnostics, KPMG/EY Adriatic banking studies, ResearchGate/Google Scholar Albanian-language payment papers, and targeted Wayback recovery of specific vendor reference pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Several intended query lines could not be executed; the cell is well covered on IFI, audit, think-tank and archive layers but thin on EBRD/IFC and on named-vendor archive recovery.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is incomplete in a known, specific way; a follow-up run with fresh budget should start from the listed unexecuted queries rather than repeating what is already covered here.

negative_findings.description: Serbian-language searching for Kosovo banking-sector research returned CBK's own sr-language mirror, a SCIndeks article, and Serbian e-banking studies about Serbia — but no Serbian-language Kosovo-focused think tank or consultancy producing banking/payments analysis.
negative_findings.result_summary: The sr-language analyst layer for Kosovo appears to be effectively absent; sr coverage rests on the CBK mirror and Serbian academic indexes.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any claim of balanced sq/sr source coverage must acknowledge that the sr side is institutional/academic only, with no independent sr analyst voice located.

coverage_gaps.description: EBRD, IFC and EIB Kosovo financial-sector diagnostics, technical cooperation project summaries and procurement notices were not searched (budget exhausted). These IFIs finance bank technology upgrades and publish project summaries naming beneficiaries.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run targeted queries and direct portal crawls: ebrd.com project summary documents filtered by Kosovo + financial institutions; ifc.org disclosed projects; EIB project list. Also check EBRD procurement notices for CBK/bank IT.

coverage_gaps.description: Wayback recovery was validated as a method (CDX confirmed working for bqk-kos.org and e-prokurimi.rks-gov.net) but was not yet run against named vendor and commercial-bank domains to recover deleted reference/press pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the actor domain list from the vendor/competitor cells, then run CDX enumeration per domain with mimetype and statuscode filters, diffing live sitemaps against archived URL sets to isolate removed evidence pages.

coverage_gaps.description: CBK's own supervisory/annual audit of licensed banks and any published on-site examination summaries were not located; only the CBK's own audited statements and stability reports were found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check whether CBK publishes supervisory reports or bank-by-bank disclosure requirements (Pillar 3 style) in sq; if not, record as a structural transparency limit.

coverage_gaps.description: Albanian-language academic literature was reached only through two university repositories; Google Scholar / ResearchGate / DOAJ sweeps in Albanian ('pagesa elektronike', 'sistemi i pagesave', 'digjitalizimi bankar') were not performed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run Albanian-keyword sweeps over Scholar, DOAJ and ResearchGate; also check the Albanian journal ecosystem (e.g. journal-uamd.org, which surfaced incidentally with an e-banking paper).

coverage_gaps.description: IMF eLibrary PDF and Deloitte full reports may be gated or bot-defended; archive.today is expected to serve CAPTCHA to automated clients. None of these were confirmed dead — only presumed friction.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat as unverified-access sources; route through a deterministic liveness pass with a browser-grade fetcher and human fallback for gated PDFs. Never attempt CAPTCHA bypass.

brief: Kosovo's analyst/auditor/archive layer is unusually strong on the supranational end and unusually thin on the commercial-consultancy end. The IMF (2020 FSSR plus the 2026 follow-up), the World Bank (Financial Sector Development project P507881, retail payment cost study, SECO-funded CBK technical assistance) and the annual European Commission Kosovo Report together give dated, citable specificity on payment-system architecture, the pending Law on Payment Services and Law on Banks, and SEPA accession status — the strategic 'why now'. Domestically, the National Audit Office (ZKA) is the highest-value under-used source: its Albanian-language IT audits of state systems name suppliers, architectures and control failures, while think tanks Riinvest and GAP supply the market-structure and consumer-cost evidence that no Big Four Kosovo study appears to provide. Web archives are the recovery backbone — Wayback CDX enumeration was confirmed working against bqk-kos.org and the e-prokurimi procurement portal, making it the practical route to deleted bank annual reports, tender attachments and vendor reference pages; this run's search budget expired before EBRD/IFC and per-vendor archive recovery could be executed.
